content.model: y_i = c_segment(i) + A_solid * full_solid_i + A_loading * full_loading_i + epsilon_i

content.uncertainty_definition: Scaled LS uses RSS/(n-rank); UTC day delete-one refits both coefficients and all surviving segment offsets, with (D-1)/D covariance. Not a new calibrated bootstrap CI.
content.limitations: Exploratory shared-observation estimate; model systematic uncertainty not included. Not a reproduction/replacement of 0.89 +/- 0.55. No independent loading detection claim or p-value.

definitions.eta_actual: alpha/(q sqrt(T) uwhite), q²=sum(n_k s_k²)/T; estimator losses are included.

content.original_text: An additional central-value check uses a Kalman filter with state (segment offset, $A$), resetting the offset at each segment and allowing a random walk reaching $5\times10^{-18}$ after 6 h. It gives $A=0.95$ for the full record; changing that scale to $2\times10^{-18}$ or $10^{-17}$ gives 0.92 or 0.99, respectively.

content.original_text: A complementary restricted wild bootstrap flips the residual sign of whole observation periods under the null. With eight periods, the smallest attainable two-sided probability is $2/256$. The resulting two-sided probabilities are 0.008 for the lunar estimate and 0.008 for the whole-template estimate.

content.original_text:
The lunar response is $A_{\rm L}=0.97\pm0.14$, consistent with the predicted amplitude (Extended Data Fig. 11a). The uncertainty is calibrated by residual resampling and represents one standard deviation (Methods). The neighbouring semidiurnal response is $0.90\pm0.29$, with a correlation of −0.32 with the lunar coefficient (Extended Data Fig. 11b); the diurnal response is $0.35\pm0.51$. A fit allowing an in-phase and a quadrature lunar template gives an amplitude of $0.98\pm0.11$ and phase offset of $-6°\pm8°$, with segment-bootstrap standard deviations. This phase test and the fixed-phase amplitude estimate describe the same observations.

The full tidal template gives $A=0.90\pm0.12$, and the combined semidiurnal band gives $0.96\pm0.12$. Semidiurnal campaign estimates are consistent ($\chi^2=3.2$, four degrees of freedom, $p=0.52$; Extended Data Fig. 3). The April record gives a whole-template response of $0.91\pm0.13$ over approximately four days (Extended Data Fig. 4).
content.replacement_text: Extended Data Fig. 11 collects the triangular-filter grouped responses, their covariance and the full-record harmonic spectrum. In the three-group fit, the diurnal coefficient is $0.35\pm0.51$; the two-band estimate in Extended Data Fig. 3b is $0.36\pm0.50$. The sampling, physical templates and uncertainty procedures are defined in “Tidal fits and uncertainty”.
content.reason: 与Results重复的全模板/月球/相位和campaign数字压缩，保留不同diurnal估计量及图的解释

content.original_text: The separate non-overlapping reduction contains 3,299 means and 545.924 member-hours in 54 segments. We use its recorded fractional-frequency means, expressed numerically in units of 10⁻¹⁸, at their stored UTC bin centres. The trial sinusoids are evaluated at these centres, following the bin-centre spectral convention; within-bin member integration and the main analysis's triangular filter are not reconstructed here. Equal spectral weights differ from the noise-based weights used for the physical amplitude estimates in that reduction.
content.replacement_text: The analyses in Extended Data Figs. 7–10 use the same non-overlapping observations and UTC bin-centre convention as Fig. 3c. Fractional-frequency values are expressed numerically in units of 10⁻¹⁸. Spectral fits use equal weights; the physical-template estimates in Fig. 3a,b use the period-dependent noise weights.
